structured_output.question: Why did a more aggressive progressive-resizing schedule (30% of steps at 20 px, 30% at 24, 20% at 28, 20% at 32) on a short (9-epoch) CIFAR-100 airbench-style run lose about 1.4 pp of accuracy relative to the milder 24→28→32 schedule (E007: 0.759 → E011: 0.745)? That drop is far more than forecast, while the time saving (5.70 s vs 7.33 s) was also larger than forecast. What mechanism makes accuracy fall off non-linearly once early resolution goes below about 24 px, or once the time spent at full resolution shrinks to 20%? Candidates include: train/test resolution discrepancy and apparent object size (FixRes), BatchNorm statistics fitted at the wrong scale, too few full-resolution steps to re-adapt late in training, interaction with the frozen 2x2 patch-whitening stem and the global max-pool head, loss of fine-grained detail that CIFAR-100 needs, and regularization strength that should change with resolution (EfficientNetV2 progressive learning). Also, which resolution schedule shapes, such as a longer final phase at full resolution, ramping regularization with resolution, or a brief BN recalibration at the test resolution, keep most of the FLOP savings without the accuracy cliff?
queries: progressive resizing low resolution training accuracy drop
train test resolution discrepancy FixRes batch normalization
progressive learning adaptive regularization image size EfficientNetV2
budgeted training resolution schedule fast convergence

mixed resolution training final full resolution fine-tuning
rubric: Measures how accuracy depends on training resolution or on the shape of a resolution schedule (minimum resolution, fraction of training at full resolution), not just a single fixed resolution
Explains or isolates a mechanism for the accuracy loss: train/test scale mismatch, BatchNorm statistics, regularization-vs-resolution coupling, or lost fine-grained information
Targets short or compute-budgeted training from scratch (few epochs, or CIFAR/ImageNet speed training), so the results carry over to a run of about 9 epochs
Proposes a schedule or fix (longer final full-res phase, BN recalibration at test resolution, resolution-dependent augmentation or label smoothing) whose cost is small and measurable
exclude: Methods that rely on pretrained weights, external data, or knowledge distillation from a pretrained teacher
Test-time augmentation or test-time resolution changes, or anything that touches the test set or changes model state during evaluation
Methods that need test-set statistics for BN recalibration (recalibration must use training images inside timed train)
Super-resolution or image-upsampling generative work unrelated to classifier training efficiency
Vision-transformer-only token-pruning methods that don't apply to small ResNet-style conv nets
Methods that need new packages beyond PyTorch 2.4 / torchvision 0.19
